info.name: TransactionTree
info.description:
This collection contains TransactionTree's RESTful APIs for digital receipt delivery, loyalty integration, coupon and promotion services, customer engagement, marketing automation, and retail data synchronization. It includes endpoints for the Retail Integration Gateway (RIG), Customer360 (C360), MessageManager (MM), and Digivize. Use this collection to test and integrate receipt issuance, customer lookup, loyalty programs, SMS/MMS and email messaging, marketing campaigns, product information (PIM), event ingestion, and transactional data feeds across in-store and eCommerce environments.

Digivize is the HMAC-signed, partner-facing marketing & engagement platform (/api/v1/external/\*): campaigns, SMS/MMS, email, contacts & lists, PIM, event ingestion, storage, validation, triggers, and webhooks. Its requests sign themselves automatically — set the DigivizeBaseURL, DigivizeApiKey, and DigivizeApiSecret variables and send.

item.name: Overview
API Credentials & Security
item.description:
ACCOUNT CREDENTIALS

This document will cover the different credentials for interacting with TransactionTree's APIs, and how to authenticate with each API.

BASIC AUTHORIZATION

The RIG, Customer360, and MessageManager APIs are protected with basic authorization over HTTPS. Basic Authorization requires the credential pair to be encoded with base64 as part of the Authorization HTTP header.

HMAC AUTHENTICATION (Digivize)

Digivize does not use basic authorization. Every request is signed with HMAC-SHA256 and carries three query parameters: key (your public API key id), timestamp (Unix seconds, which must be within ±300s of server time), and signature (lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 of the canonical request, keyed by your secret). Digivize has a pre-request script that builds all three automatically — it uses body-binding mode for JSON bodies (adding the X-Api-Signature-Includes-Body: 1 header and signing a SHA-256 of the raw body), standard mode for GETs, and the reduced canonical for POST /transactions. To use it, set DigivizeApiKey and DigivizeApiSecret and choose a tenant via DigivizeBaseURL. Never place key, timestamp, or signature in the request body — auth travels in the query string only. Multipart uploads (sms/media, storage/upload) are not auto-signed and must be signed manually.

Credentials Defined

Credential Name Description Usage

passwordThe password for your VRG API credentialsVRG

X-tenant-KeyUnique identifier that represents a single merchant in C360.C360
accessTokenKeyBase 64 encoded key that is generated by C360.C360
client_idThe client id for your MessageManager API credentialsMM
client_passwordThe client password for your MessageManager API credentialsMM
access_tokenAccess token generated by the MessageManager APIMM
DigivizeBaseURLPer-tenant Digivize host, e.g. https://digivize.sandbox.example.com (your tenant host is issued with your credentials).Digivize
DigivizeApiKeyPublic API key id identifying the caller; sent as the key query parameter.Digivize
DigivizeApiSecretCaller secret used to compute the HMAC-SHA256 signature. Never sent on the wire; keep it local.Digivize

API CREDENTIALS

All TransactionTree API access must be requested and approved. Please submit your request to support@transactiontree.com.

Welcome to TransactionTree's Developer Docs

TransactionTree offers RESTful Web Services to allow the transfer of data to and from our infrastructure. This is provided through four different services.
Retail Integration Gateway (RIG)

Digital receipts, content, triggered emails, and customer lookup.
Customer360 (C360)

Loyalty, Coupons, and Promotions
MessageManager (MM)

Text Messages, two way communication, and remote payments.
Digivize

Marketing & engagement platform: campaigns, SMS/MMS, email, contacts & lists, PIM, event ingestion, storage, validation, triggers, and webhooks.

Digivize

Digivize is a modern, HMAC-signed REST API served per-tenant under /api/v1/external/* (e.g. https://digivize.sandbox.example.com). It is organised into 15 groups: Campaigns, Contacts, Email, Event Ingestion, Campaign Lists, Organization, PIM, Product Notifications, SMS / MMS, Storage, Templates, Transactions, Triggers, Validation, and Webhooks.

Unlike the other three services, Digivize authenticates with HMAC-SHA256 (not basic auth). Every request carries three query parameters — key, timestamp, and signature — which the folder's pre-request script computes for you. Set DigivizeBaseURL, DigivizeApiKey, and DigivizeApiSecret, pick a tenant, and send. See API Credentials & Security for details.

item.description:
The eReceipt service ingests transaction data into the Retail Integration Gateway (RIG). The RIG accepts **any type of transaction data** — not only digital receipts — so a single integration can carry the full transaction record.

## Schemas

TransactionTree supports two schemas for submitting transaction data.

### TTDR 3.2.2 (XML) — current

The TransactionTree Digital Receipt (**TTDR**) schema is the current production XML schema.

- **Browse on GitHub:** [https://github.com/TransactionTree/transactiontree-schemas/blob/main/vrg/3.2.2/TTDR-3.2.2.xsd](https://github.com/TransactionTree/transactiontree-schemas/blob/main/vrg/3.2.2/TTDR-3.2.2.xsd)
    
- **Raw XSD (download / reference):** [https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TransactionTree/transactiontree-schemas/refs/heads/main/vrg/3.2.2/TTDR-3.2.2.xsd](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TransactionTree/transactiontree-schemas/refs/heads/main/vrg/3.2.2/TTDR-3.2.2.xsd)
    

### ORAE (JSON) — next generation

**ORAE** is TransactionTree's next-generation transaction schema, defined in JSON.

> **ORAE schema access is by request.** The ORAE schema is not publicly published. To receive the ORAE schema and integration details, request access from your TransactionTree representative.

item.name: Response Codes
item.description:
Type Code Reason Description
Error 400 Bad Request Bad syntax in the client request
Error 401 Unauthorized This is used when the resource is restricted to certain authenticated users.
Error 403 Forbidden User made a valid request but the server is refusing to serve the request, due to a lack of permission to access the requested resource
Error 404 Not Found User is able to communicate with the server but it is unable to locate the requested file or resource
Error 405 Method Not Allowed This is used when the request is well-formed and the resource it asks for does exist, but the request method (such as GET or POST) is not appropriate to the resource.
Error 410 Gone Status code is used if the server knows, through some internally configurable mechanism, that an old resource is permanently unavailable and has no forwarding address
Error 500 Internal Server Error The server cannot process the request for an unknown reason
Error 501 Not Implemented This is returned when the HTTP request method (such as PUT or DELETE), the API method in some cases, has not yet been implemented.
Error 502 Bad Gateway Means that the server is not receiving a valid response from the backend servers that should actually fulfill the request
Error 503 Service Unavailable Means that the server is overloaded or under maintenance
Error 504 Timeout Means that the server is not receiving a response from the backend servers within the allowed time period.
Error 505 HTTP Version Not Supported The HTTP protocol version used in the request.
Error 701 Invalid username or password The username or password provide is invalid.
Error 702 Invalid Security Token The security token provided is not valid.
Error 703 Security Token Expired The security token provided has expired.
Error 705 General Error This is a general error.
Error 708 Missing File File was not attached in the message.
Valid 800 Upload Success The upload has been excepted by the VRG.
Valid 800 Logout Success Logout was success.
Valid 800 Email Address The email address that the VRG has on file.
Valid 801 Email address with preference The email on file has a receipt preference saved.
Valid 802 NoEmail No email is on file for the id provided.
Valid 803 Email but no Receipt preference An email is on file for the id provided but no receipt preference has been saved
Valid 804 Bounced The email on file for this id has bounced prior
Valid 805 Email Blocklist The email on file has been added to the blocklist and is no allowed. Ask user to contact a service rep.
Valid 806 Format Emails that fail RFC syntax protocols
Valid 807 Spamtrap These emails are believed to be spamtraps and should not be mailed. We have technology in place to determine if certain emails should be classified as spamtrap. We don't know all the spamtrap email addresses, but we do know a lot of them.
Valid 808 Abuse These emails are of people who are known to click the abuse or spam links in emails, hence abusers or complainers. We recommend not emailing these addresses. If you wish to email display a message targeted at these email addresses.
Valid 809 Forbidden An id has been provided that is not allowed to be emailed to.
Valid 810 Multiple Emails Multiple Email addresses found for ID
Valid 811 No MX Record The domain that an email is going to can not receive emails.
Valid 812 Domain Corrected The email domain has been automatically corrected. Please have customer check email address again.
Valid 814 Valid Email Format The email address has passed all format and block list checks.
Valid 815 Domain Blocked This domain is blocked by TransactionTree and no emails will be sent.
Valid 817 Phone Prefix Blocked The prefix of the phone number is not allowed.
Valid 818 Phone Area Code Blocked The area code of the phone number is not allowed.

request.description:
The coupon authentication service enables a client application to validate a coupon number with C360. The coupn number is generated based on LUHN Formula and is always unique.
There are five coupon status codes that may be returned.
  1. COUPON_AVAILABLE: The coupon is valid and available to use.
  2. COUPON_UNAVAILABLE: The coupon code is wrong or not valid.
  3. COUPON_EXPIRED: This coupon has expired.
  4. COUPON_REDEEMED: The coupon has already been redeemed.
  5. COUPON_AUDITED: The coupon has already been redeemed and there is a matching order in the system.

L2DESCRIPTION3 Addl Long Description of the Product based on the Content Type in ERP or Different Locale LONGTEXT
L2DESCRIPTION4 Addl Long Description of the Product based on the Content Type in ERP or Different Locale LONGTEXT
L2DESCRIPTION5 Addl Long Description of the Product based on the Content Type in ERP or Different Locale LONGTEXT
PRODUCTTYPE* Product type - Allowed (FINISHED_GOOD / SERVICE /DIGITAL_GOOD / RAW_MATERIAL ) VARCHAR(20)
DEFAULTSHIPMENT Default Shipment Box Type (YOUR_PACKAGING) - See List of other Options in Appendix VARCHAR(20)
SMALLIMAGEURL Absolute or Relative URL path of the Images (if any folder and same name of the Image with different resolution) VARCHAR(20)
MEDIUMIMAGEURL Absolute or Relative URL path of the Images (if any folder and same name of the Image with different resolution) VARCHAR(20)
LARGEIMAGEURL Absolute or Relative URL path of the Images (if any folder and same name of the Image with different resolution) VARCHAR(20)

WIDTH Width of the Product based on Unit of Measure (UOM) decimal(18,6)
UNITQTY Quanity in inventory INTEGER

request.description:
Inbound party-change push for external CRMs (e.g. OFBiz). Idempotently upserts a contact resolved by stable identity in priority order: `external_ref` (unique per brand), `uuid`, `bormc_customer_id`, `phone`, then `email`. **At least one** of those identity fields is required (otherwise **422**). A match returns **200** (`created: false`) and lists the changed keys in `updated_fields`; a soft-deleted match is restored (`restored: true`). When nothing matches, a new contact is created and **201** is returned (`created: true`) — but a create requires a `phone` (the global SMS-routing key), so an identity-only miss with no phone is **422**. Only the supplied profile fields are written (an omitted field is left untouched); `uuid` is never mutated and `bormc_customer_id` is set only when currently empty. An `external_ref` already used by another contact in the same brand yields **422**; a suppressed/malformed phone yields **422**; a brand the caller is not authorized for yields **403**. The optional `idempotency_key` is recorded for request correlation — the endpoint is idempotent by construction (replaying any sync converges to the same contact state).

Imported from the OpenAPI spec `digivize-openapi-08172026.json` (generated from `#[ApiDoc]` attributes; source of truth is `php artisan api:docs:openapi`).

**Base path:** `/api/v1/external/*`  •  **70 endpoints** across 15 groups.

## Authentication — HMAC-SHA256
Every request carries three query parameters — `key`, `timestamp`, `signature` — added automatically by this folder's **pre-request script**. Set these variables (collection or environment):

| Variable | Set to |
|---|---|
| `DigivizeBaseURL` | e.g. `https://digivize.sandbox.example.com` |
| `DigivizeApiKey` | your public API key id |
| `DigivizeApiSecret` | your caller secret (kept local, never synced) |

Tenants: each customer has its own `<tenant>` host, issued with your credentials

The signer uses **body_binding** mode for JSON bodies (adds `X-Api-Signature-Includes-Body: 1` and signs a SHA-256 of the raw body), **standard** mode for GETs, and the reduced **transactions** canonical for `POST /transactions`. Multipart uploads (`sms/media`, `storage/upload`) are NOT auto-signed — sign those manually.

// collect existing query params except the three auth params; trim + drop empties (server normalises)

// transactions mode: sign only key, timestamp, transaction_id
canonical = buildQuery({ key: key, timestamp: ts, transaction_id: (txid == null ? '' : String(txid)) });
